title: Interest Entropy: Rethinking Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation with Interest Uncertainty

problem.claim: Sparse interaction data makes user preferences difficult to learn in sequential recommendation.

gap.claim: Uniform augmentation and alignment ignore distinct sequence interest structures, causing semantic discrepancy and semantic bias.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces Interest Entropy to measure the diversity and density of interest distributions and studies augmentation effects on sequence semantics.
The authors report that only a small fraction of sequences are stable under perturbation, with stability concentrated among low- or high-entropy sequences.
The paper proposes IERec, a mutual-retrieval augmented contrastive learning method guided by Interest Entropy.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Spectral analysis indicates that positive alignment can cause low-entropy sequences to overlook niche interests and high-entropy sequences to amplify interest-irrelevant signals.
IERec reportedly avoids harmful semantic discrepancy and reduces semantic bias, leading to improved performance.
Using Interest Entropy to guide contrastive learning reportedly further improves existing contrastive-learning sequential recommendation methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation must learn user preferences from sparse behavioral interactions, and contrastive learning has shown promise.
Uniform augmentation and alignment overlook differences in sequence interest structure, producing semantic discrepancy and semantic bias.
Interest Entropy is used to analyze augmentation effects; few sequences are stable under perturbation, and alignment can distort niche or irrelevant interests.
IERec retrieves semantically similar sequences with complementary entropy and concatenates them into positive views while excluding medium-entropy sequences from augmentation.
The authors report reduced semantic discrepancy and bias, improved performance, and gains for existing contrastive-learning methods.

unknowns: No datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or evaluation protocol are specified.
The abstract does not define the Interest Entropy formula or the mutual retrieval procedure in detail.
